set.approach: Start at the Summit Lake shelter and travel up the Caribou Glacier toward the Caribou/Parade divide, heading north-west. Beyond the divide you reach the Parade Glacier by one of two ways: steep snow and ice down the west edge, or a rappel from the bolted anchor by the saddle on the east. The climb starts on the East Face just right of an obvious deep gully above the Parade Glacier; the wall across from that gully sheds rock, so do not linger beneath it.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit plateau of the North Tower, and the standard way down starts from an obvious rappel point across the plateau. Rappels lead down to the gap separating the two towers, then a rotten gully leads to a hanging snowfield whose crossing is exposed and may be icy. Beyond it you can scramble or keep rappelling slabs and cliffs from established anchors. The anchors on the standard route are of modest quality, and rockfall in the gully is a hazard. Rappelling the route itself is possible but most of the lower face has no anchors, so it means setting your own down a very tall wall.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach and the standard descent; area page confirms Summit Lake shelter and Caribou to Parade Glacier; Wikipedia confirms the standard descent is the original east-side route for climbs on other faces. Counts (hours, rappels) left out as only one source.
